correctness.rationale: Fourier character orthogonality is proved for arbitrary prime-power fields; each isotropic decomposable wedge has q(q²−1) ordered presentations, with dependent pairs correctly subtracted. For every alternating frequency B, the multiplier is q^(n−2)(J(B)−1)−δ with J a nonnegative integer and δ=(q^(n−2)−1)/(q²−1). The strict inequality 2δ<q^(n−2) yields nonvanishing and the lower bound; an explicit nilpotent Jordan-block pencil attains J=1 in all characteristics. The trivial character and isotropic-pair count attain the upper bound. The two embedded standalone scripts actually checked full spectra for q=2,n=6 and two smaller normalization cases, samples at q=3,n=6, and extension-field samples at q=4,n=4; none is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed advance is the exact all-prime-power nearest-zero Fourier multiplier and invertibility condition number in ambient symplectic dimension at least six, including all least-stable pencil frequencies. Cardinali–Giuzzi establish the support geometry and projective codeword intersection/weight framework, and explicitly determine extreme minimum weight and low-dimensional enumerators, not the nearest-zero multiplier. Their formulas could be leveraged in a derivation, so general counting and dimension-four data are not claimed as original. Searches identified distinct coordinate-restriction/Grassmannian projection and unrestricted alternating rank-two convolution results, none of which implies the stated sharp bound. Residual historical priority from broader code-weight/association-scheme theory is material but not currently decisive.
residual_risks: A previously proved general symplectic line-code weight distribution or association-scheme theorem could imply the nearest-zero inequality without using convolution terminology.

The highly related indexed Fourier/Plücker and Grassmann harmonic findings were compared via published indexed scientific summaries, not their full texts. Their published claimed domains differ, but summary-level inspection does not rule out unadvertised corollaries.
Independent mathematical validation and complete closed multiplicity enumeration are not performed.

value.rationale: The full cone of nonzero totally isotropic decomposable bivectors is a geometrically canonical support, not an arbitrary finite slice. Exact invertibility and optimal ℓ² condition number q^n−1 across all finite fields and dimensions n≥6 quantify worst-case deconvolution stability; the integer spectral gap and complete criterion for least-stable pencils explain the operator’s nontrivial lack of zeros and identify extremizing frequencies. A precise structural, infinite-family endpoint result is useful independently of a full spectral multiplicity table. The original dimension-four enumerator and routine Fourier orthogonality alone do not answer this stability question.
